common_name: Siloam Virginia Henson Daylily (Rose-Pink Siloam Series Dwarf Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade; Siloam Virginia Henson forms a compact, dwarf clump suited to the front of a border.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade. Bred by Pauline Henry as part of her celebrated Siloam series of dwarf daylilies bred at Siloam Springs, Arkansas, Virginia Henson bears rose-pink flowers with a bold rose-red eyezone above a green throat, held on compact scapes over a low, tidy clump of grassy foliage. Its dwarf stature and richly patterned eye have made it a long-favored edging plant among Siloam collectors. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain heavy flowering.

common_name: Yabba Dabba Doo Daylily (Ruffled Tangerine-Orange Diamond-Dusted Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade; Yabba Dabba Doo carries a heavy diamond-dust sheen that sparkles brightly in direct sunlight.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade. Bred by Jack Carpenter, Yabba Dabba Doo bears heavily ruffled, glowing tangerine-orange flowers edged in a lighter gold band, with a strong diamond-dust sparkle across the petal surface that catches the light on sunny afternoons. This tetraploid blooms in a full midseason flush above a vigorous, floriferous clump. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain strong bloom production.

common_name: Julie Newmar Daylily (Ruffled Cream-Pink Gold-Edged Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade; Julie Newmar carries a fine gold picotee edge that stands out against its pale petals.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade. Bred by Jack Carpenter and named for the actress, Julie Newmar bears large, heavily ruffled, cream-pink flowers edged in a fine gold picotee band above a green throat, opening on well-branched scapes through a strong midseason display. Its clean pastel color and crisp ruffled edge have made it a popular garden and show cultivar. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Wineberry Candy Daylily (Ruffled Wine-Purple Candy Series Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade; Wineberry Candy belongs to David Kirchhoff's small-flowered 'Candy' line, sharing its compact scapes and heavy bud count with siblings such as Strawberry Candy and Blackberry Candy.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade. Bred by David Kirchhoff as part of his small-flowered 'Candy' line, Wineberry Candy bears ruffled, deep wine-purple flowers with a lighter lavender watermark above a green throat, held on compact, well-branched scapes over a tidy, floriferous clump. Like its better-known siblings Strawberry Candy and Blackberry Candy, it is valued for its dependable rebloom and edging-scale habit. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain heavy flowering.

common_name: Coyote Moon Daylily (Lavender Eyezone Spider-Variant Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade; Coyote Moon carries a heavy diamond-dust sheen across its petals that glitters in direct sun.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade. Bred by Curt Hanson, Coyote Moon bears pale lavender, spider-variant flowers marked with a deeper purple eyezone above a green throat, its narrow, gracefully twisting petals catching a heavy diamond-dust sparkle in direct sunlight. This tetraploid blooms in a full midseason display above a vigorous clump. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain strong bloom production.
